fr.elements: Main Building; Secondary Building; Vehicle Parking Area; Internal Drive Aisle; Outdoor Storage Area; Material Storage Area; Access Road; Dumpster Enclosure; Landscaped Area; Open Area
fr.considerations: Multiple Access Points; Outdoor Storage; Multiple Structures; Limited Rear Access
fr.recommendations:
• Mark each access point with a visible address or building identifier so responders can quickly confirm their entry location.

• Mark the rear of the main building with a unit or building identifier visible from the access road serving that side.

• Keep the outdoor storage area organized so a clear path remains between stored materials and building walls.

• Keep the material storage area clear of building entrances and fire department connections.

• Post a site map at the primary access point showing building locations, secondary building position, storage areas, and all access points.

• Mark the internal drive aisle with directional signage to guide responders between the main building, secondary building, and storage areas.

• Keep the dumpster enclosure positioned so it does not block vehicle movement along the internal drive aisle.

• Identify the access road serving the rear of the property with signage so responders can locate it without prior site knowledge.

• Keep the vehicle parking area from blocking the internal drive aisle during normal operations so emergency vehicles can move between structures without obstruction.

wildfire.conditions: Large Paved Area; Tree Cluster; Scattered Trees; Open Paved Area; Woody Debris; Limited Vegetation Separation; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Multiple Access Routes; Open Terrain
wildfire.recommendations:
• Remove woody debris accumulations visible on the property — piled or scattered dead wood can ignite quickly and carry fire toward buildings.

• Thin the tree cluster to reduce the concentration of branches and foliage in one area, and keep low-hanging limbs trimmed up from the ground.

• Trim lower limbs from scattered trees near buildings to reduce the chance of fire climbing from the ground into the tree canopy.

• Where vegetation separation between trees or shrubs and buildings is limited, pull back or remove plants that are growing close to exterior walls, eaves, or entries.

• Keep the large paved areas and open terrain clear of any vegetation or debris that may encroach over time — these open areas provide useful separation between vegetation and buildings and should be kept free.

• Maintain existing multiple access routes clear of vegetation overhang and debris so they remain passable for emergency vehicles.
